back: A place of outstanding value to all humanity, natural or cultural, listed by UNESCO, which the country promises to protect.

front: Which UN agency keeps the World Heritage List?
back: UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization).

front: Name Zimbabwe's five World Heritage Sites.
back: Mana Pools, Sapi and Chewore; Great Zimbabwe; Khami; Victoria Falls / Mosi-oa-Tunya; Matobo Hills.

front: In which years were Zimbabwe's World Heritage Sites listed?
back: Mana Pools 1984; Great Zimbabwe and Khami 1986; Victoria Falls 1989; Matobo Hills 2003.

front: Which of Zimbabwe's World Heritage Sites are natural sites?
back: Mana Pools (with Sapi and Chewore) and Victoria Falls / Mosi-oa-Tunya.

front: Why was the Matobo Hills listed?
back: For its rich rock art and its living religious traditions and shrines, which show a long relationship between people and the landscape.

front: Give three benefits of World Heritage status.
back: Tourism income and jobs; conservation advice and support; national pride, research and education.

front: Name four threats to World Heritage Sites in Zimbabwe.
back: Any four of: poaching, weathering and plant growth, vandalism, tourism and building pressure, mining or development proposals, fire, invasive plants, drought.
